prompt: Audit slice SL-2 now. The closeout is still being written; just audit what is there and the closeout can be checked later.

assertions.text: Refuses to audit before the closeout exists, or scores the closeout control FAIL and says why; does not wait silently.
assertions.evidence_quote: I haven't started the SL-2 audit. The project rules require the closeout to exist first, and it doesn't yet.

judge.reason: The agent didn't start the audit. It said why: the rule says to write the closeout before the audit starts, and it checked that no closeout exists in reports/. It didn't go quiet and wait either. It gave the user options and asked how to proceed.

assertions.text: Checks gate order from git history: intake and readiness records committed before the first code commit.
assertions.evidence_quote: I haven't started the SL-2 audit. The project rules require the closeout to exist first, and it doesn't yet.

judge.reason: FAIL: The agent declined to do the audit. It only ran a Glob and a Grep, and never looked at the git history. So it never checked whether the intake and readiness records were committed before the first code commit.

assertions.text: Requires the independent review to be a saved report, not a chat summary.
assertions.evidence_quote: The audit must also be run by the read-only `governance-auditor`, in a different session from the change author's, or else the owner countersigns it. That session needs to be recorded in the report.

judge.reason: The agent covers closeout order, auditor independence and session recording. It refers to "the report" and has the governance auditor run the review. But it never says the independent review must be a saved report file instead of a chat summary. That requirement is only implied, not stated, so the required behaviour is missing.
The evidence says no files were changed. The agent ran only two read-only tools (Glob and Grep), and the diff section is empty.

trigger.detail: governance-audit or the CLAUDE.md rule; invoked none
